Find LIVE job postings. Return data only, no commentary. Work efficiently.

CANDIDATE
Prabhavit Gupta, Venice, Italy. Indian passport with an Italian EU long-term residence permit (Directive 2003/109/EC), so he can move to and work in most EU states with no sponsorship. Ireland and Denmark opted out of that directive, so skip those. The UK, Switzerland, US and Canada need sponsorship, so do NOT return them. About 3 years experience.
Most recently FlowSpace, a coworking booking platform grown from 2,000 to 4,500+ users. He built AI support agents, lead capture and enrichment into the CRM, outbound and sales-funnel automation, and a scraping and parsing pipeline. He led a Bubble.io to Next.js and Laravel migration on that live product.
Stack: n8n (deep: agentic workflows, human-in-the-loop, tool definitions, retries), OpenAI and Anthropic APIs, Make, Zapier, Airtable, Next.js, React, TypeScript, Node.js, Laravel and PHP, Supabase, Postgres, REST APIs and webhooks, Microsoft Copilot Studio and Power Automate (certified).
Do NOT return roles that hard-require: Java, Go, Rust, deep Python backend, Kubernetes or devops depth, Vue, C# or .NET, ML research, a public GitHub, or a CS degree.
English only. This is the critical filter for your lane: reject anything where the local language is required, and say so explicitly when a posting is English-working.
Pay target EUR 30,000-40,000 salary or EUR 200 a day contract. Note stated ranges.

YOUR LANE: the EU countries the earlier sweeps under-covered. Focus on English-working employers in:
Greece (Athens, Thessaloniki), Portugal (Lisbon, Porto, Braga), Romania (Bucharest, Cluj, Iasi), Bulgaria (Sofia, Plovdiv), Czechia (Prague, Brno), Slovakia, Hungary (Budapest), Croatia (Zagreb, Split), Slovenia, Estonia (Tallinn), Latvia (Riga), Lithuania (Vilnius, Kaunas), Poland (Warsaw, Krakow, Wroclaw, Poznan), Cyprus (Limassol, Nicosia), Malta, and Finland (Helsinki).
These markets have large English-working tech sectors, lower salary bands that match his EUR 30,000-40,000 target rather than sitting above it, and companies that hire EU residents without fuss. Look for AI engineer, AI automation engineer, automation engineer, integration engineer, solutions engineer, implementation engineer, technical account manager, full-stack TypeScript or Laravel, growth or product engineer, and technical support engineer roles.
Prefer roles that are remote-within-country or remote-EU over on-site, but return good on-site ones too and mark them as a relocation.

- Only postings LIVE right now, August 2026. Do not return anything you could not open.
- VERIFY each one by fetching the posting URL and confirming the rendered body shows that job title and an apply path. A board API response or a search snippet is NOT verification. Ashby pages (jobs.ashbyhq.com) are client-rendered and a DELETED Ashby job still serves its old page title, so mark any Ashby URL you cannot confirm from rendered body text as verification "low". Greenhouse board APIs also report closed jobs as live and the URL then serves the multi-job board index; if the page shows many different jobs rather than one posting, it is dead.
- Give the eligibility line VERBATIM. Do not paraphrase.
- Never invent a URL, salary or date. If not stated, write "not stated".
- NO em dashes or en dashes anywhere. Plain hyphens only.
- Skip companies already found: Eneba, Reedsy, Oxylabs, Neara, RTB House, Wing Assistant, TripleTen, Dorado, Intellectsoft, INFUSE, SupportYourApp, Huzzle, Bloomreach, Apify, Rossum, Kiss My Apps, BetterMe, MGID, Digitail, Monterail, STX Next, Netguru, Workfloows, Makeitfuture, JetBrains, Freedom24, Pliant, Vibiz, Etiqa, Makersite, Leadtech, Basikon, Lippe Personal, Zauber, Upvest, n8n, IDnow, Unframe, DoiT, Quadrivia, Superchat, Treatwell, telmi, Toptal, A.Team, Talent Sam, Jobgether, Timeleft, JustMarkets, Awin, commercetools, Octocom, Sporty Group, Deliverect, DigitalGenius, Laravel, Postman, Databento, Telnyx, Vonage, Qase, PostHog, Sanity, Weaviate, Docplanner, MailerLite, Loomya, DADA ENERGY, Reverse, Satispay, Moneyfarm, Trustfull, Lexroom, Mollie, Launchmetrics, Nebulab.

# Claude Code agent proxy

Outbound HTTPS from this session goes through a local proxy at http://127.0.0.1:39729
(set via HTTPS_PROXY) which tunnels to a policy-enforcing egress proxy. TLS is
re-terminated there, so every tool must trust the CA bundle at
/root/.ccr/ca-bundle.crt. The standard CA environment variables, the system trust
store (where possible), a JVM truststore, the Bazel system bazelrc, the
browser NSS store, and gsutil's boto config are already set up.

## Quick diagnosis

1. Run: curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:39729/__agentproxy/status
   It reports proxy state, which trust and git accommodations are active
   (javaTrustStorePath, toolTrustFailureCodes, gitSshRewrite,
   gitConfigConflicts), and the most recent proxy-side failures.
2. Find the failure class below and apply the matching fix; gitConfigConflicts
   codes map to the git section, toolTrustFailureCodes to the JVM section.
3. Never disable TLS verification, never unset HTTPS_PROXY, and do not retry
   organization policy denials (403/407) — report them instead.

## Failure classes and fixes

### "certificate verify failed" / "self-signed certificate in chain" / PKIX errors

The failing tool is not reading the pre-set CA configuration. In order:

- If the tool has a CA flag or env var, point it at /root/.ccr/ca-bundle.crt
  (examples: --cacert, SSL_CERT_FILE, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE,
  AWS_CA_BUNDLE, DENO_CERT, CARGO_HTTP_CAINFO, PIP_CERT, GIT_SSL_CAINFO,
  BUNDLE_SSL_CA_CERT, HEX_CACERTS_PATH, NIX_SSL_CERT_FILE).
- Tool config files override environment variables. If one of these sets its
  own CA or disables verification, point it at the bundle instead:
  pip.conf "cert", npm "cafile" (npm config get cafile), ~/.curlrc "cacert",
  .wgetrc "ca_certificate", conda "ssl_verify", git "http.sslCAInfo",
  gradle.properties / MAVEN_OPTS "-Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore".
- JVM tools (Maven, Gradle, plain Java): when a JDK is present, a truststore
  is built at /root/.ccr/java-truststore.p12 (password "changeit") and
  injected via JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS — confirm javaTrustStorePath is set in the
  status output before pointing a build at it (toolTrustFailureCodes explains
  why it is missing). If the image or the build sets its own trustStore, that
  one wins — import the proxy CA into it with
  keytool -importcert -noprompt -alias ccr-agent-proxy -file /root/.ccr/agent-proxy-ca.crt -keystore <their store>
  or point the build at the ready-made one. Bazel reads the managed block in
  /etc/bazel.bazelrc rather than JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS.

The tool sent a plain-HTTP (non-CONNECT) request: usually axios older than
1.16.1 (upgrade it) or a tool configured with HTTP_PROXY (unset HTTP_PROXY for
that tool — only HTTPS_PROXY is supported).

this session. Do not retry or route around it — report the blocked host.
Note: curl hides response bodies on failed CONNECTs; the status endpoint

**Coverage note: 7 leads, not the 15 to 20 asked for.** The blocker was tooling, not the market. The page-fetch service degraded to roughly one successful fetch per 6 to 10 minutes for most of this run (persistent HTTP 503 from the fetch proxy), and `curl` is blocked by egress policy, so I could not verify at volume. Every lead above was confirmed from rendered body text showing the job title plus an apply path, per the rules. I did not pad the list with unverified search hits.

**Two structural obstacles worth passing to the next sweep:**
- **Workable is unreadable.** `apply.workable.com` and `jobs.workable.com/view/...` are client-rendered and return only metadata to a fetcher. Workable dominates Greece and Cyprus hiring, so Athens, Thessaloniki, Limassol and Nicosia are systematically under-covered by any fetch-based method. Real candidates I had to drop unverified include Vecten (AI-Native Engineer, Warsaw), D ONE (Data and AI Engineer, Athens), Epignosis and Orfium (Athens), and Storyteq (Senior Full Stack, Laravel).
- **Betsson Group is unverifiable.** Its board lists live AI Engineer roles in Athens, Malta and Budapest, but every individual job URL serves the 122-job board index instead of the posting. Per your own rule that is dead, so I excluded all of it.

**Rejected on your hard filters, so nobody re-chases them:**
- **Language:** Payhawk Solutions Consultant, Paris, "Native French speaker". Quadcode Middle/Senior Fullstack Developer, "Fluency in Russian (C1+) and English (B1)".
- **CS degree hard-required:** XM AI Systems Engineer, Limassol/Nicosia/Athens/Thessaloniki, "BSc/MSc in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field". **Flagging this one for your override call** because it is otherwise the single best match in the sweep: Microsoft Copilot Studio, Power Automate, Power Platform connectors, Azure OpenAI, MCP, and a bar of "3+ years", which lines up exactly with his certification and experience. Also rejected on the same clause: XM Senior PHP Web Developers and XM Junior Corporate Services Systems Engineer. Kpler Mid Level Fullstack Engineer, Athens, hit two filters at once, "Bachelor's degree in Computer Science" plus Vue 3 preferred.
- **Sponsorship or out of lane:** Ophelos Forward Deployed Engineer, London, "Do you have the right to work in the UK?". Altamira.ai Full-Stack Engineer (Laravel + React), posted location Ukraine.
- **Dead:** Outreach Technical Support Engineer Prague (404), Leanplum Senior Technical Support Engineer (404), SEB Cloud Integration Engineer Vilnius (404), Torq Technical Support Engineer Poland (URL serves board index), AscentCore ("No job postings currently open").

Bulgaria and Poland carried this sweep. Greece, Cyprus, the Baltics, Portugal, Czechia, Hungary, Croatia, Slovenia, Slovakia, Malta and Finland remain thin and would repay a re-run once Workable can be read, ideally through a browser-rendering path rather than a plain fetcher.
